items.title: 2027 Has ARRIVED 🎉 | The Official WHOOP UCI MTB World Series Calendar! 🗓️
items.description:
The stage is set for another incredible year of racing, bringing together some of the biggest names in mountain biking at the sport's most iconic venues! 🌍🏆

From legendary circuits and tracks to breathtaking mountain landscapes, the 2027 season promises another year of world-class racing, fierce rivalries, and unforgettable moments across Cross-country and Downhill! 💪

👀 There's plenty to get excited about, with fan-favourite Les Gets, Haute Savoie featuring earlier in the season and Val di Sole, Trentino making its highly anticipated comeback to the calendar! Two iconic venues ready to deliver even more incredible racing in 2027! 🇫🇷🇮🇹

Alongside our European icons, the season rounds out in North America with Soldier Hollow and Whistler! 🇺🇸🇨🇦 After making their debuts in 2026, both venues delivered incredible crowds, high-stakes drama and thrilling racing. Now they're back to bring the heat once again as the season reaches its final stages! 🔥

New challenges, familiar battlegrounds, and another season of the world's best riders going head-to-head for UCI World Cup glory! 🏆

📆 Get the dates in your diary! Which round are you most excited for? 👇

items.title: We Blind Tested MTB Tires With Asa Vermette
items.description:
Can a Downhill World Cup champion tell the difference between mountain bike tires without knowing what he's riding?

We teamed up with Continental Tires and 2026 Downhill World Cup overall champion Asa Vermette for a blind tire test at Whistler Bike Park to find out just how much tire casing and rubber compound affect performance on the trail.

With three different Continental Kryptotal tire setups, we put downhill, enduro, and trail casings and compounds head-to-head. The catch? Neither rider knows which tires they're using.

Presented By: Continental

20 years after his first World Cup DH race at the iconic Schladming Bike Park, Rob brings Tom back to the Austrian Alps! Experience what it’s like to conquer one of the world's most legendary downhill courses aboard modern DH rigs.

items.title: World Cup Speed Comes at a Price - Commencal Supreme V5.2 Tested
items.description:
All Vital Downhill Bike Tests - https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLLiDwPfY-lhyKX6qJehUoemu-DtWI7jf1

The latest version of Commencal’s Supreme V5.2 was developed and won races during the 2025 season before being released to the public this summer. The changes are visually minor, but pivot points were moved, and the bike's personality was altered. The changes clearly worked: Max Alran scored his first Elite win this season, and Vali Holl wrapped up her 5th Elite title two rounds early. 

The bike is obviously a rocket ship, but what enables it to go so dang fast? What’s it like to manage and direct that speed when you don’t have World Cup-level abilities? Time to find out…

items.title: What Happens When You Ignore the Rules of Downhill Bike Design?
items.description:
One of the most unconventional bikes on the Downhill World Cup circuit is proving its worth.

After leaving a factory team to pursue his own vision of the ultimate downhill race bike, Reece Wilson teamed up with Gamux to challenge conventional bike design. With a Gates belt drive, gearbox drivetrain, radical geometry, and an unusual cockpit setup, almost nothing about this bike follows the traditional formula.

Made in partnership with Gates
https://go.gates.com/GBD-100K-BELTED-PURSE.html

items.title: After Years of Prototyping, We Finally Get to Ride It - Norco Team DH
items.description:
All Vital Downhill Bike Tests - https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLLiDwPfY-lhyKX6qJehUoemu-DtWI7jf1

For the past five years, we’ve patiently waited for Norco to release the production version of its next downhill bike. We watched multiple versions raced at World Cups, including Gracey Hemstreet racking up three wins on the bike in 2025. And now that it's finally here, it offers plenty to talk about.

With plenty to dive into, we spent a few days testing the Team DH in the Whistler Bike Park to see what all these years of development have produced.
